registration_note: Registered by the implementer in the same session that wrote the planner and before any corpus-wide run; only one recorded study (shared-endpoint-v4-002) had been replayed as a smoke test.
design: retrospective: every configuration draws each requested role from the same recorded report, so configurations differ only in which roles (and, with curtailment, which pairs) they would have used

profile.role: profile built from study 000 of each topology and address family, applied to every other study of that family

primary_metrics.accuracy: classification statement equals the topology ground truth; unresolved is wrong; every planned study stays in the denominator
primary_metrics.traffic: measured transmitted packets (SYNs plus RST cleanup) summed over the roles a configuration used

gates.G1_no_accuracy_loss: every adaptive configuration is correct on every study where fixed is correct
gates.G2_traffic: adaptive-curtailed transmits fewer packets in total than fixed
gates.G3_honest_coverage: a statement or port is tested only when a role that measures it was run; fixed tests every recorded role
gates.G4_profile_invalidation: a profile is valid exactly when applied to a study of the topology it was built from
gates.G5_profile_inference: in valid applications every profile-inferred statement equals the value fixed measured for that study

counterexamples: every study where an adaptive configuration's classification, direction, cooldown or rate-limiter statement differs from fixed is listed, whether or not a gate fails
limitations: Retrospective: a prospective adaptive run would see different pairs; recorded pairs stand in for them.
Retrospective curtailment's duration ends at the next pair's first send, an upper bound.
One shared-kernel Linux lab with SYN token-bucket limiters only; repetitions are not independent hosts.
IPv6 studies recorded only main and same-port, so the null control was never available for them.
